rule: The broadest true term comes first; at most two blends follow; anything narrower than a dictionary term goes in subgenres. A term never appears together with its own parent or ancestor. Use drama as the frame only when no other root is true.

action-adventure.definition: A journey or campaign driven by physical conflict and escalating obstacles.
action-adventure.promises: Momentum, competence under pressure, and set pieces with clear geography.
action-adventure.avoid: Stakes that reset between set pieces.

alternate-history.definition: History diverged at a known point, and the world that followed.
alternate-history.promises: The divergence traced through institutions and daily life.
alternate-history.avoid: A changed past that changes nothing else.

comedy.definition: Events arranged to produce laughter through timing, reversal and character.
comedy.promises: Jokes that arise from who people are.

coming-of-age.definition: A protagonist crossing into a new stage of life.
coming-of-age.promises: An irreversible change in how they see themselves.
coming-of-age.avoid: A lesson stated instead of lived.

cosmic-horror.definition: The universe as indifferent and unknowable.
cosmic-horror.promises: Scale that dwarfs the characters and knowledge that damages.
cosmic-horror.avoid: A threat that can be fought on human terms.

crime.definition: The commission and consequence of a crime from inside it.
crime.avoid: A criminal world that runs on convenience.

cyberpunk.definition: High technology, low life, corporate power over bodies and data.
cyberpunk.promises: Texture, and a price paid for every augmentation.

drama.definition: Character conflict with serious stakes and no genre machinery.
drama.avoid: Melodrama unearned by what came before.

dystopian.definition: A society organised to oppress, seen by those it oppresses.
dystopian.promises: The system's logic and its cost.
dystopian.avoid: A regime that exists only to be toppled.

erotica.definition: Sexual experience as the subject of the story.
erotica.promises: Explicit intimacy rendered as experience, not implication.
erotica.avoid: Fading out at the moment the genre exists to depict.

espionage.promises: Information as the currency of power.
espionage.avoid: Gadgets doing the work of judgement.

fantasy.definition: A story in which magic and impossible beings are integral, not incidental.
fantasy.promises: Wonder, and a world that takes its own magic seriously.
fantasy.avoid: Magic invented at the moment it is needed.

folklore.definition: Fairy tale, folk tale, legend and myth told in their own register.
folklore.promises: The shape and logic of the traditional tale.
folklore.avoid: A folk tale explained until it stops being one.

gothic.definition: Decay, inheritance and a place that behaves like an antagonist.
gothic.avoid: Atmosphere with no buried history behind it.

heist.definition: A plan, a crew, an execution and its unravelling.
heist.promises: Competence, timing and the plan surviving contact.
heist.avoid: A plan that succeeds because the author needs it to.

historical.definition: A real period the author did not live through, rendered with fidelity to its material life.
historical.promises: Period-true constraint on what people can do and know.

horror.definition: Dread and the violation of safety.
horror.promises: Consequence, and the unknown kept unknown for as long as it can be.
horror.avoid: Dread the story never has to pay off.

literary.definition: Interiority and language carry the weight.
literary.promises: Sentences that earn their place and change that happens in perception.
literary.avoid: Plot as a pretext for style.

magical-realism.definition: The impossible treated as ordinary by everyone in the story.

mystery.definition: A question of fact answered by evidence.
mystery.promises: An investigation whose answer the evidence supports.
mystery.avoid: An answer that rests on information the story withheld.

noir.definition: Moral compromise in a world that stays corrupt.
noir.promises: A case, a compromised protagonist and an ending that costs.

paranormal.definition: The supernatural intrudes on an otherwise ordinary contemporary world.
paranormal.promises: The intrusion has terms of its own, learned by contact.
paranormal.avoid: The supernatural as a scare with no reason.

political.definition: Power contested through institutions, factions and public claims.
political.promises: Every move has a constituency and a cost.

portal-fantasy.definition: Someone from the ordinary world enters the magical one.
portal-fantasy.avoid: The ordinary world as a discarded prologue.

post-apocalyptic.definition: Life after the collapse of a civilisation.
post-apocalyptic.promises: Scarcity as the shaping fact of every choice.
post-apocalyptic.avoid: Abundance appearing when the plot needs it.

procedural.definition: The work is the plot: cases, shifts, protocols and the people who keep them.
procedural.promises: Fidelity to how the work is actually done.
procedural.avoid: Expertise that appears only when convenient.

psychological.definition: Thoughts, feelings and motive matter at least as much as outward events.
psychological.promises: What a character believes shapes what happens.

retelling.definition: An existing tale or property retold with a changed frame.
retelling.promises: Recognisable beats, and a reason for this telling.
retelling.avoid: A retelling that adds nothing the source did not already do.

romance.promises: A central love story resolved in an emotionally satisfying, optimistic ending.
romance.avoid: A tragic or ambiguous ending, and resolution by declaration alone.

satire.definition: Institutions and manners exaggerated to expose them.

science-fiction.definition: A change in what is possible, and the story of its consequences.
science-fiction.promises: Consequences of the premise taken seriously.

slice-of-life.definition: Ordinary days rendered closely, with small stakes that matter.
slice-of-life.avoid: Importing a plot engine from another genre.

steampunk.definition: An industrial-age world with anachronistic technology and its social order.
steampunk.promises: The machinery has a maker and a cost.

superhero.promises: Power with a code, and consequences in a world that notices.

tragedy.definition: A fall that follows from character.
tragedy.promises: Inevitability that the reader sees before the protagonist does.
tragedy.avoid: A fall caused by accident alone.

urban-fantasy.definition: The mundane world with a hidden, rule-governed magical society inside it.
urban-fantasy.promises: The rules of that layer and the cost of crossing it.
urban-fantasy.avoid: The mundane world as a mere backdrop.

war.definition: Armed service and organised violence, and the people inside them.
war.promises: The weight of orders, losses and logistics.

western.definition: Frontier, law at the edge of reach, and the cost of violence.
